events.title: Troy falls, according to ancient Greek reckoning
events.description: Greek chronographers, notably Eratosthenes, dated the fall of Troy to 1184 BCE, and later writers placed it in late April. The legend, told in Homer and Virgil, shaped European literature for millennia.
events.html: Greek chronographers, notably Eratosthenes, dated the fall of Troy to 1184 BCE, and later writers placed it in late April. The legend, told in Homer and Virgil, shaped European literature for millennia.

events.title: The Abbasid caliph al-Qahir is deposed and blinded
events.description: Al-Qahir, the nineteenth Abbasid caliph, was deposed and blinded, and his nephew al-Radi succeeded him. Al-Radi's reign marked the end of the caliph's political power and the rise of military strongmen competing for the title of amir al-umara.

events.title: Charles V defeats the Schmalkaldic League at Mühlberg
events.description: Emperor Charles V and the Duke of Alba crossed the Elbe near Mühlberg, surprised the Protestant army of Elector John Frederick I of Saxony and captured the elector. The battle decided the Schmalkaldic War.
events.html: Emperor Charles V and the Duke of Alba crossed the Elbe near Mühlberg, surprised the Protestant army of Elector John Frederick I of Saxony and captured the elector. The battle decided the Schmalkaldic War.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, marries the Dauphin Francis in Paris
events.description: Mary, Queen of Scots, married Francis, Dauphin of France and heir to the French throne, at Notre-Dame de Paris. Francis became King of France in 1559 and, as Mary's husband, was also King of Scotland until his death in 1560.

events.title: Congress establishes the Library of Congress
events.description: President John Adams signed the act moving the government to Washington and setting aside $5,000 for books for Congress. The collection became one of the largest libraries in the world.
events.html: President John Adams signed the act moving the government to Washington and setting aside $5,000 for books for Congress. The collection became one of the largest libraries in the world.

events.title: Russia declares war on the Ottoman Empire
events.description: Russia went to war in support of the Balkan Christians. The peace that followed made Romania, Serbia and Montenegro fully independent and created an autonomous Bulgaria.
events.html: Russia went to war in support of the Balkan Christians. The peace that followed made Romania, Serbia and Montenegro fully independent and created an autonomous Bulgaria.

events.title: Ottoman authorities arrest Armenian leaders in Constantinople
events.description: Hundreds of Armenian intellectuals and community leaders were rounded up and deported, most later killed. The date marks the start of the Armenian genocide, in which around a million people died.
events.html: Hundreds of Armenian intellectuals and community leaders were rounded up and deported, most later killed. The date marks the start of the Armenian genocide, in which around a million people died.

events.title: Irish rebels launch the Easter Rising in Dublin
events.description: Irish Volunteers and the Citizen Army seized the General Post Office and proclaimed an Irish Republic. The Rising was crushed within a week, but the executions that followed turned opinion towards independence.
events.html: Irish Volunteers and the Citizen Army seized the General Post Office and proclaimed an Irish Republic. The Rising was crushed within a week, but the executions that followed turned opinion towards independence.

events.title: Space shuttle Discovery launches the Hubble Space Telescope
events.description: Hubble was carried into orbit by Discovery and deployed the next day. A flaw in its mirror was corrected in 1993, after which it transformed astronomy.
